chunks.arabic_text: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ رَشَادَ بْنِ خَثِيمٍ، الْعَامِرِيُّ، الْهَلَالِيُّ. زَيْدِيّ، يَدْخُلُ حَدِيثُهُ فِي حَدِيثِ أَصْحَابِنَا، ضَعِيفٌ، فَاسِدٌ.

translations.en: Ahmad ibn Rashad ibn Khuthaym, al-'Amiri, al-Hilali. Zaydi, his hadith are included among the hadith of our companions. Weak, corrupt.

en.summary: Ahmad ibn Rashad ibn Khuthaym is characterized as a Zaydi narrator whose hadith are integrated into the corpus of 'Aṣḥābuna (our companions), yet he is classified as weak (da'if) and having corrupt narration (fasid). This classification highlights the nuanced Shia approach to evaluating narrators from other sects, where theological affiliation (Zaydi) influences the assessment of reliability even when their reports are utilized within the primary chain of transmission.
en.seo_question: What is the status of Ahmad ibn al-Rashad's hadith in Shia scholarship?

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions (referring to prominent Shia narrators)
